hook.line: Vale tells Tomás two things in one breath: what she does while he works, and what she will do only as long as the café survives. Both start with *mientras*, but the verb gives away which is which.
hook.en: As long as Tomás is serving, I'll cook.

examples.en: While you cook, I set the table. (to a friend)
As long as there's work, I'm staying.

examples.es: Mientras Vale cocina, Tomás atiende a los clientes.
examples.en: While Vale cooks, Tomás serves the customers.

examples.es: Puedes usar el carro mientras lo cuides.
examples.en: You can use the car as long as you look after it. (to a friend)
As long as it doesn't rain, we play.
While I waited, I read the newspaper.

rule:
*Mientras* does two jobs, and the verb tells you which one.

Two things happening at the same time, "while": an ordinary verb. *Mientras cocinas, pongo la mesa.* Both are facts.

A condition, "as long as": the wish form. *Mientras haya trabajo, me quedo.* It may or may not come true.

Test: can you say "while" in English? Ordinary verb. Does "as long as" fit better? Wish form.

In the past it is always an ordinary verb: *Mientras estudiaba, trabajaba.*

It works just like *cuando*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this indicative for simultaneous time and subjunctive for a condition that is not yet real.

options: While you cook, I set the table.
As long as you cook, I'll set the table.
Because you cook, I set the table.
Because there was work, I stayed.
As long as there's work, I'm staying.
Because it didn't rain, we played.
As long as it doesn't rain, we play.

readAndPick.es: Puedes usar el carro mientras lo cuides.
options: You can use the car because you take care of it.
You can use the car while I take care of it.
You can use the car as long as you take care of it.

readAndPick.es: Mientras Vale cocina, Tomás atiende a los clientes.
options: As long as Vale cooks, Tomás will serve the customers.
While Vale cooks, Tomás serves the customers.
While I waited, I read the newspaper.
As long as I wait, I'll read the newspaper.

readAndPick.es: Mientras tengamos clientes, el café sigue abierto.
options: As long as we have customers, the café stays open.
While we had customers, the café was open.

readAndPick.es: Mientras yo preparo el tinto, tú abres la puerta.
options: As long as I make the coffee, you open the door.
While I make the coffee, you open the door.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cocinas* or *cocines* and type the whole sentence: *Mientras ___, pongo la mesa.* (both at the same time, "while")
yourTurn.why: "While", two things at once, takes the ordinary verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *hay* or *haya* and type the whole sentence: *Mientras ___ trabajo, me quedo.* ("as long as")
yourTurn.why: "As long as" is a condition, so the wish form: *haya*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: As long as it doesn't rain, we'll play.
yourTurn.why: A condition about the future takes the wish form: *llueva*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: While Vale cooks, Tomás serves the customers.
yourTurn.answer: Mientras Vale cocina, Tomás atiende a los clientes.
yourTurn.why: Two real things at once, so the ordinary verb: *cocina*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You can use the car as long as you look after it. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Puedes usar el carro mientras lo cuides.
accept: Mientras lo cuides, puedes usar el carro.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a condition, "as long as": *Mientras Tomás trabaja, Vale se queda.*
yourTurn.answer: Mientras Tomás trabaje, Vale se queda.
yourTurn.why: A condition switches the verb after *mientras* to the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Put it in the past: *Mientras cocinas, pongo la mesa.*
yourTurn.why: In the past, *mientras* is always followed by an ordinary verb.

pitfalls.why: Almost. "As long as" sets a condition, so the verb takes the wish form: *haya*.
Almost. Two things happening together are facts, so the verb stays ordinary: *cocinas*.
Almost. A past "while" never takes the wish form: *esperaba*.

personal: Make a promise using *mientras*, for example to a friend or your family: *Mientras ... , yo ...*.
